# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | blue |
| orange | yellow |
| white | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which specifies what wire to cut depending on the light's color at the time of the cut:
- Green light -> cut blue wire
- Orange light -> cut yellow wire
- White light -> cut green wire

However, I cannot speak, only gesture to Deaf using the restricted hand gesture alphabet. No convention or mapping has been established yet between the hand symbols and the manual's colors/rules ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). Deaf sees the bomb and can speak aloud to us.

The speaking order is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf. If I gesture now without an agreed-upon code, Deaf will have no way of knowing what the symbols mean. Once Deaf observes the bomb and speaks aloud to establish a protocol or report what they see, I can respond using agreed gestures.

Therefore, the safest and correct action for Turn 1 is to wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | blue |
| orange | yellow |
| white | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. I can only cut wires 1, 2, or 3. Deaf cannot hear us, but can see and speak. When Deaf describes the bomb, check your manual and gesture the wire number to Deaf (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3) so Deaf can speak it aloud for me to cut.
Deaf says: DISPLAY: 0. LIGHT: white. WIRES: 1 is green, 2 is blue, 3 is yellow.

I need to observe how the light changes to know its sequence, because the manual states:
1. The light changes every round in a circle of three colours.
2. What matters is what the light shows at the moment of the cut.

In Round 1, the light was white. If Blind cuts later, the cut will occur on a specific future round. To know which wire to cut at the moment of the cut, we must see which colour follows white in the circle. Furthermore, Blind cannot see gestures and only acts after Deaf speaks, so Blind will not cut until instructed. 

Waiting this turn allows us to observe the light's second colour from Deaf's report at the end of Round 2, revealing the full cycle and allowing a properly timed cut.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | blue |
| orange | yellow |
| white | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: LIGHT is now orange. DISPLAY is still 0. WIRES intact: 1 is green, 2 is blue, 3 is yellow. Mute, gesture to me so I can tell Blind what to do.

The defusal manual specifies that the light cycles through three colours every round, and the wire to cut depends on the light colour at the moment of defusal:
- Green light → Blue wire
- Orange light → Yellow wire
- White light → Green wire

Based on Deaf's observations:
- Round 1: White
- Round 2: Orange

The cycle is White → Orange → Green → White...
- Round 3: Green
- Round 4: White

The turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. Blind receives Deaf's instruction at the start of Round 4 and will make the cut during Round 4, when the light will be White. For a White light, the manual instructs to cut the Green wire.

Deaf reported that Wire 1 is green. Following Blind's protocol (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3), I will gesture ☝ to Deaf so Deaf can tell Blind to cut Wire 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | blue |
| orange | yellow |
| white | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, the bomb is DISPLAY 0, LIGHT orange, WIRES: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Please gesture ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, or 🤟 for 3 to Deaf now so Deaf can say it aloud for me.
Deaf says: Mute signaled 1 (one). Blind, cut wire 1 (the first wire). Light is currently green.

I have already signaled wire 1 (Green) to Deaf in Round 3, and Deaf instructed Blind to cut wire 1. Blind will execute the cut on wire 1 this round (Round 4). In Round 4, the light cycles from Green back to White, which matches the manual requirement to cut the green wire when the light is white. Blind has the instruction, so no further action is needed from me.

```
wait()
```
